title: [Bug]: White frames appear when adding BrowserView with already loaded page
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [X] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [X] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

20.1.4

### What operating system are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

Ventura 13.2

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

~~In my use case, I need to keep `BrowserView`s in memory and switch them.~~
~~To switch I use `removeBrowserView` and `setBrowserView` APIs like this:~~

```
    win.removeBrowserView(view1);
    win.setBrowserView(view2);
```

~~I expect that this switching will be experienced by users as tab switching in the browser. For example, if you open two tabs~~
~~https://<redacted-host>/ & https://<redacted-host>/docs/latest/api/app, and will start switching between them you will notice that the website header remains black (for this specific example with electronjs.rg).~~

In my use case, I need to add `BrowserView` with an already loaded page to the window. When I do this I am able to notice a white glitch even though I set another color as a background color for the window.
This bug is not reproducible if hardware acceleration is turned off. (`app.disableHardwareAcceleration()`)

### Actual Behavior

It works as desired on Windows 11.
On MacOS some white frames appear and make the user's experience less native.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7069867/217718946-abd92f15-baec-43e8-a5c9-4c1bd3d2c0f8.mov

Can we get it fixed or give me suggestions on how I can perform a workaround, please?

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/0c99927c913ac5971facd861dd656d8b

### Additional Information

_No response_

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Does `addBrowserView` + `setTopBrowserView` (alternatively move views out of bounds to hide them) work?

FWIW I don't see any flashing on Ubuntu. Also Electron 20 is EOL.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Hey @participant1 Thanks for your reply! `addBrowserView` + `setTopBrowserView` works. However, pages may have transparent background and it causes the pages to overlay each other: This is not something desired

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Either make it white via https://<redacted-host>/docs/latest/api/browser-view#viewsetbackgroundcolorcolor-experimental or maybe try my other suggestion and translate the "invisible" views off-screen using `setBounds`. These are the same techniques you'd use in CSS for high-performance flicker-free switching of items (e.g. `translate(x,y)` them off-screen).

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Hello,
I wanted to clarify the steps to reproduce via another fiddle: https://gist.github.com/reporter/ad54907ca6e8d1167c5bde6a6bf389ac

Every time when I add a new `browserView` on top of another `browserView` the white glitch appears.
I want to fix it somehow without having all the `browserView`'s attached. After I made some measures I found out the app consumes more resources when the window has attached multiple `browserView`'s at the same time.

In my use case, we have a tab management feature, which does not look native when the user switches between tabs.

comments.author: reporter
reporter
comments.body:
I noticed that `setTopBrowserView` was added to Electron [here](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/27007) by @participant11 with the note:

> Removing and re-adding a view also works but has the problem of introducing a noticeable flicker.

cc @participant11 @participant10 Do you think we can fix it somehow in Electron? After a quick reading of Electron's source code, I think this is a Chromium bug. If you have any recommendations on what should be our next steps it will be very helpful!

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
I also found an error logged every time the view flickers on Fiddle.

```
[39915:0317/095700.282818:ERROR:shared_image_manager.cc(267)] SharedImageManager::ProduceOverlay: Trying to Produce a Overlay representation from a non-existent mailbox.
[39915:0317/095700.282829:ERROR:skia_output_device_buffer_queue.cc(354)] Invalid mailbox.
```

comments.author: participant2
participant2
comments.body: Upon further testing, the workaround above only works on high-end Macs. Glitches will still appear on lower-end devices where the amount of resources is less. 😢

comments.body:
Also, I tried to use a short delay (100ms) before showing new contents after it is attached.
I placed sources in [this PR](https://github.com/reporter/electron/pull/3/files) and it seems to work well.

However, it reminds me the same hack @participant2 described above. Probably it will not work in lower-end devices where the amount of resources is less.

I am interested if there is any other way to wait for content to be painted rather than use hard-coded delay? 🤔
